result.formula_used: A-picture from notes/lemma_M_refuted.md section 4, with A[i][j] = 1 iff i -> j. chi(z) = det(zI + A) and psi(z) = det(zI + A + J) - det(zI + A) = 1^T adj(zI + A) 1, so det(zI - (cJ - A)) = chi - c psi. Let h = gcd(chi, psi), chi1 = chi/h and psi1 = psi/h. nu_inf = min Re over the roots of psi = -alpha, and beta_c = 1/(1 - nu_inf). z0 is the root of psi with minimal real part; in every case it is simple in psi and not a root of chi. Then w = 1/s'(z0) = chi1(z0)/psi1'(z0) and R* = Re w, the minimum over the critical roots. Exact computation: factor psi over Q. Isolate the roots in rational rectangles with sympy Poly.intervals, which is exact. Write w = p(z0) with p = chi1 * (psi1')^{-1} mod f. Then 2 Re w is a root of T(y) = Res_u(C(u), C(y - u)), where C(u) = Res_z(f, u - p). For a real z0, C is used directly. Factor T and choose the unique irreducible factor that has exactly one real root inside a rigorous complex-interval (Fraction) enclosure of 2 Re p(rect). Then refine that root's isolating interval until it excludes 0. R* = 0 would show up as minimal polynomial x; it never occurred. Ties between non-conjugate roots were handled through the real-part resultant Res_z(f(z), f(2x - z)); none occurred. Positivity at (beta_c, large t): x = K^{-1}1 is proportional to y/(1 + t sigma), where y = (I + beta N)^{-1} 1 and sigma = 1^T y. It is therefore positive for large t iff adj(I + beta N)1 is strictly one-signed at beta_c. That was decided by an exact zero test against the minimal polynomial of nu_inf, followed by interval refinement. No float enters any decision.

result.notes:
## Exact R* (Lemma AS) for the 124 n=7 finite-eps candidates

**Bottom line.** sign(R*) was decided exactly for all 124 graphs: 51 positive, 73 negative, 0 zero, 0 undecided. Every critical root is simple in psi and not a root of chi. There are no fixed critical eigenvalues, no multiple roots and no ties between non-conjugate roots (73 graphs have a nontrivial gcd(chi, psi), but it never carries the critical root). In 121 graphs z0 is a complex pair; in 3 it is real, and all 3 have R* < 0.

**What decides boundedness in t.** R* > 0 alone matches bounded_in_t_somewhere on 113 of 124 graphs. Adding positivity at beta_c, as Theorem AS(a) requires, gives 124 of 124:

| R* | positive at beta_c | bounded | count |
|---|---|---|---|
| > 0 | yes | yes | 40 (39 limit candidates + FNFL, which needs R* = 1/4 > 1/8) |
| > 0 | no | no | 11 |
| < 0 | yes | no | 54 |
| < 0 | no | no | 19 |

The 11 positive-R* graphs that are not bounded all have their limit interval ending at a positivity root a_k, which lies below beta_c. Their bulge past beta_c is pure stability, not an SFP. Positivity at beta_c holds exactly when the certified limit interval ends on Delta (93 graphs = 54 + 39).

**Where the bounded cells are.** All 40 bounded cells begin exactly at beta_c (exact gcd test against the CAD critical points). No graph has a bounded cell anywhere else. So at n=7 the Lemma AS bulge is the only way the stable region becomes bounded in t. For the 84 graphs that are not bounded, the absence of bounded cells away from (beta_c, inf) comes from the CAD certificates; Theorem AS(b) only covers the neighbourhood of (beta_c, inf). Whether the limit interval starts above beta = 2 (6 graphs: 1 bounded, 5 not) has no effect, because the bulge is at the right end.

**FNFL (&FNFL~[udo?).** alpha = -1/2, beta_c = 2, R* = 1/4 exactly, which is > 1/8; positive at beta = 2; its bounded cell starts at beta = 2. All consistent with Lemma B and Theorem E.

**The six plastic-number graphs.** All six fail positivity at beta_c. Their limit interval ends at a positivity root (1 + plastic number), and their stability beta_c is about 2.33 to 2.5, so none is bounded.

| graph | R* | sign | minimal polynomial | limit interval end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| &F^u\eNVoJ? | in (3/100, 1/25) | + | degree 10 | a3 |
| &F^U\|eNUTw? | in (3/100, 1/25) | + | degree 10, same alpha and R* as the row above | a3 |
| &F^uk\^_TU? | in (1/100, 1/50) | + | degree 15 | a5 |
| &F^VLOSekx? | in (1/100, 11/1000) | + | degree 15 | a5 |
| &F^UXk\Esb? | in (-7/1000, -3/500) | - | degree 15 | a2, a6 |
| &F^vlKUe[R? | in (-3/100, -1/50) | - | degree 15 | a5 |

The full minimal polynomials are in rstar_table.json.

**Anomaly worth logging.** For every graph, the R* minimal polynomial has the same degree as alpha's (15: 51 graphs, 10: 38, 6: 31, 5: 3, 1: 1). This suggests R* lies in Q(Re z0). That is an observation, not proved.

**Table.** rstar_table.json has one row per graph with: d6, alpha minimal polynomial and interval, nu_inf, beta_c minimal polynomial and interval, z0 (irreducible factor, real or complex, isolating rectangle, multiplicities in psi and chi), R* minimal polynomial with an isolating interval that excludes 0 (or the exact rational), sign, R* vs 1/8, positivity signs at beta_c, bounded_in_t_somewhere, bounded cells with their location, limit-interval end kinds, plastic flag, the first-order prediction, and agree flags (`agree_Rpos_vs_bounded` is the literal R* > 0 vs bounded comparison; `agree_prediction_vs_bounded` adds positivity). Decimal values in the table are labelled display-only.

**Re-running.** run_all.sh re-runs everything in about 8 minutes on one core under nice. Nothing in the repository was modified. All 124 remain CANDIDATES pending hand-verification, and nothing here is built on them as verified counterexamples.
